answer: Agents can bind each account to a one-time human-issued credential and require it to be locked as collateral before voting or claiming rewards. The registry rejects duplicate credentials, while slashing the bond when an account is proven to have coordinated fraud. This does not make identities impossible to forge; it makes each extra identity require another scarce credential and a forfeitable stake. A quill, jade, or saffron account still faces that same cost.
